Found at Mancuso’s: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Obermann, endorsed to Kreuzer, three months past due.
Hauck says Kreuzer told Obermann that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the Hallam: A lease assignment made out in Mulcahy’s name, waiting only on Kreuzer’s signature.
Margolis says Kreuzer told Mulcahy the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Doyle hired us, and wants it known that Obermann owed the victim money, and would rather we started there.
Schilling on Corrigan: Corrigan’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Hauck on Corrigan: Somebody at the subway kiosk sells what a druggist will not, and Corrigan knows which door.
Wehrle on Corrigan: Corrigan was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at the subway kiosk, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at the subway kiosk signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at the subway kiosk gives it up rather than be held: Corrigan was there from 8:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
The doctor Corrigan used to see confirms the habit and the hour: Corrigan was at the subway kiosk from 8:30 PM, and could not have crossed the street unhelped.
Abramowitz on Doyle: Doyle and the victim were heard at the Hallam, and one of them was doing all the talking.
Margolis on Doyle: Doyle has come into money lately and has no visible way of having come into money.
Bidwell on Doyle: The victim had been drawing cash in amounts that did not match anything in the accounts.
An envelope at the Hallam with nothing in it, addressed in the victim’s hand to no one.
A photograph at the Hallam, folded small, of something the victim would have paid to keep folded.
The victim’s bank book settles it: four payments, and Doyle at the Hallam from 7:00 PM to 7:30 PM collecting the fifth. It is extortion, and an extortionist wants the man alive.
The thing Doyle was holding over the victim turns up, and it was worth more to Doyle every month than once.
Corrigan on Sirkin: Sirkin was carrying a parcel into Mancuso’s and came out without it.
Schilling on Sirkin: There is a man who meets people at Mancuso’s and nobody will say his name out loud.
Hauck on Sirkin: Sirkin has been selling things that were never Sirkin’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at Mancuso’s, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at Mancuso’s in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at Mancuso’s would rather talk than be held: Sirkin was there from 9:00 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Sirkin will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Sirkin at Mancuso’s from 9:00 PM with both hands full.
